intro: I am a computational social scientist studying how AI and algorithmic systems shape the information environments people encounter and how these environments can be redesigned to support better decision-making. For a complete list of papers and presentations, see my CV.

themes.title: Interventions for Healthier Information Environments
themes.description: Rather than only documenting the harms of platforms and AI, I build and rigorously test interventions that change what people encounter, and measure what they actually do. In my dissertation project, I apply this approach to three goals: reducing engagement with untrustworthy sources, bridging partisan divides, and building trust in elections.

themes.title: Algorithms & Recommender Systems
themes.description: Ranking and recommendation algorithms are core infrastructure of the information environment: they decide what people see, and when. I study how these systems can be designed to be more prosocial and pro-democratic.

subthemes.title: Alternatives to Engagement Maximization
subthemes.description: Engagement-optimized ranking rewards what people click, not what they value. Through user studies, LLM-based recommenders, and open ranking competitions, I design and evaluate user-centered alternatives.

themes.title: Science of Science: Knowledge Infrastructure
themes.description: Science has its own information environment. The same questions—what gets seen, by whom, and through which systems—apply to scholarly knowledge: publication languages, search and indexing systems, data archives, and AI tools shape which research gets produced and how it is found and built upon.
